title: NY State Assembly · District 86
area: West Bronx, including University Heights, Morris Heights, Mount Eden, Kingsbridge, Tremont and Fordham.

context.text: Incumbent Yudelka Tapia is unopposed in the Democratic primary. Maria Diaz defeated Shery Olivo 57.5%-35.8% in the June 23, 2026 Republican primary; Olivo separately advanced unopposed on the Conservative Party line, so both remain on the November ballot.

candidates.name: Yudelka Tapia

priorities.text: A just recovery from COVID-19 that uplifts working families, communities of color and immigrants, including support for small businesses.
Preserving and expanding affordable housing, including building 100% sustainable permanent affordable housing and reforming the 421-a tax program.
Protecting tenants by stopping evictions, building on the state's rent regulations, and holding bad landlords accountable.
Fighting for NYCHA residents through major infrastructural investment without privatization.

positions.summary: Her 2020 campaign issues page says she will fight to stop evictions, build upon the state's rent regulations, hold bad landlords accountable, and protect tenants from housing discrimination and harassment.
Her 2020 campaign issues page says she supports gun safety laws and initiatives to keep communities safe.
positions.quote: keep our communities safe by supporting gun safety laws and initiatives

positions.summary: Her 2020 campaign issues page says police budgets have grown at the expense of community programs and need to be cut, with the money shifted to community programs, jobs and mental health care.
positions.quote: police budgets have grown at the expense of community programming and it’s clear they need to be cut

candidates.researchNotes: Tapia has not completed a 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, and her sponsored-legislation table on Ballotpedia is rendered via JavaScript and was not accessible to this research tool. Her campaign website's issues page appears to date from an earlier campaign cycle (its language centers on COVID-19 recovery) but is her most recent publicly available statement of positions found; no distinct 2026-specific platform page or official record of sponsored bills could be located.

candidates.name: Maria Diaz
candidates.researchNotes: Re-checked https://ballotpedia.org/Maria_Diaz_(New_York) (2026-09-25): she has not completed the 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey and no campaign website is linked from her infobox. A web search and her GoodParty.org listing (https://goodparty.org/candidate/maria-diaz/new-york-state-assembly-district-86) turned up no biography, priorities, or policy statements beyond the primary result. Ballotpedia lists no prior elected office for her. Re-checked 2026-10-21: still no biography, website or Candidate Connection survey found.

candidates.name: Shery Olivo

priorities.text: Education and youth empowerment: expanding access to quality schools, literacy initiatives and mentorship programs.
Economic growth and opportunity: supporting small businesses and creating pathways to good-paying jobs.
Public safety and youth support: holding repeat violent offenders accountable and investing in youth programs.

candidates.researchNotes: Olivo completed a 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey; Ballotpedia lists no prior elected office for her. Her campaign website contains templated content unrelated to her candidacy alongside her genuine biography and issue statements; only the material clearly specific to her campaign was used here.

sources.title: Shery Olivo for New York State Assembly District 86

researchNotes: Both Diaz and Olivo advanced to the general election because Diaz won the Republican primary while Olivo held a separate, uncontested Conservative Party line. Diaz has essentially no public footprint beyond her primary win; no website, biography or statements were found for her. Only Olivo has completed a 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey. Diaz has no biography beyond the Ballotpedia listing, so her background is left empty.
